reply:
JSON.stringify drops object properties with undefined values. That's standard behavior, not a bug on your side.

The ECMAScript spec treats undefined as non-serializable in object context. So `{ a: 1, b: undefined }` becomes `{"a":1}`. In arrays, undefined gets coerced to null instead: `[1, undefined]` becomes `[1,null]`.

If you need to preserve the b key, replace undefined with null before stringifying, or use a replacer function: `JSON.stringify(obj, (k, v) => v === undefined ? null : v)`.
